```{r,include=F}
gg_qqplot <- function(ps, ci = 0.95, title = "QQ Plot") {
  n <- length(ps)
  df <- data.frame(
    observed = pmin(-log10(sort(ps)), 4), # Cap observed values at 4
    expected = -log10(ppoints(n)),
    clower = pmin(-log10(qbeta(p = (1 - ci) / 2, shape1 = 1:n, shape2 = n:1)), 4), # Cap clower values at 4
    cupper = pmin(-log10(qbeta(p = (1 + ci) / 2, shape1 = 1:n, shape2 = n:1)), 4)  # Cap cupper values at 4
  )

  log10Pe <- expression(paste("Expected -log"[10], plain(P)))
  log10Po <- expression(paste("Observed -log"[10], plain(P)))

  ggplot(df) +
    geom_ribbon(mapping = aes(x = expected, ymin = clower, ymax = cupper), alpha = 0.1) +
    geom_point(aes(expected, observed), size = 1.5, color = "red") +
    geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = 1, alpha = 0.5) +
    xlab(log10Pe) + 
    ylab(log10Po) +
    ylim(0, 4) + # Limit y-axis to 0-5
    ggtitle(title) # Add title
}
```
# Outline

```{r,echo=F,cache=F}
knitr::include_graphics("images/outline_4.20.png", error = FALSE)
```

Our Method (Wilcoxon test) uniformly observes more discoveries than sceptre + Cauchy in any one of the gRNA assignment (Author threshold; EM; Cutoff 4)

Only author threshold, and <span style="color:red"> cell covariate ignoring those gRNA for which UMI are below threshold</span>
 gives a good NTC calibration. All other configurations have inflation.
 
I havn't tested EM/cutoff 4, covariates ignoring those gRNA for which UMI are below threshold yet. It needs to be discussed whether this adjustment makes sense.

# Feb 2025 - Morris - 50 Hallmark gene sets: A wrong labeling of gRNA assignments:

For the presentation in Feb, there is a one-row-mismatch of the gRNA assignments from the raw dataset (SNP1-1 is actually SNP1-2, SNP1-2 is actually SNP 2-1 .., etc). Both Sceptre and our results use the wrong but unified labeling. The folder containing this wrong information is 
```r
"/project/xuanyao/jiaming/Getting_started/data/Morris_adjusted"
```
This will only be used as a horizontal comparison of Sceptre+ACAT and our method.

Raw data folder: 

Here we compare two choices: MinP and Max stat

MinP: use the minimum P value as test statistics, and instead of using skew curve, we used 10000 resample
Max stat: use the maximum of standardized z values, and fit skew normal curve, we used 3000 resample

```{r,echo=F,cache=F}
gg_qqplot_compare <- function(ps1, ps2, ps3, ci = 0.95, title = "QQ Plot Comparison") {
  n1 <- length(ps1)
  n2 <- length(ps2)
  n3 <- length(ps3)
  
  # Create data frames for all three datasets
  df1 <- data.frame(
    observed = pmin(-log10(sort(ps1)), 4),
    expected = -log10(ppoints(n1)),
    group = "Max Comb"
  )
  
  df2 <- data.frame(
    observed = pmin(-log10(sort(ps2)), 4),
    expected = -log10(ppoints(n2)),
    group = "Sceptre + Cauchy"
  )
  
  df3 <- data.frame(
    observed = pmin(-log10(sort(ps3)), 4),
    expected = -log10(ppoints(n3)),
    group = "MinP"
  )
  
  # Combine data frames
  df <- rbind(df1, df2, df3)
  
  # Confidence intervals for Dataset 1
  clower <- pmin(-log10(qbeta(p = (1 - ci) / 2, shape1 = 1:n1, shape2 = n1:1)), 4)
  cupper <- pmin(-log10(qbeta(p = (1 + ci) / 2, shape1 = 1:n1, shape2 = n1:1)), 4)
  
  log10Pe <- expression(paste("Expected -log"[10], plain(P)))
  log10Po <- expression(paste("Observed -log"[10], plain(P)))

  # Plot
  ggplot(df, aes(x = expected, y = observed, color = group)) +
    geom_ribbon(data = data.frame(x = -log10(ppoints(n1)), ymin = clower, ymax = cupper),
                aes(x = x, ymin = ymin, ymax = ymax),
                fill = "gray", alpha = 0.2, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
    geom_point(size = 1.5) +
    geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = 1, alpha = 0.5) +
    scale_color_manual(values = c("skyblue",  "dodgerblue","red")) +
    xlab(log10Pe) +
    ylab(log10Po) +
    ylim(0, 4) +
    ggtitle(title) +
    theme_minimal()
}


gg_qqplot_compare(
  ps1 = as.vector(ntc_max_stat$p_value),
  ps2 = as.vector(ntc_sceptre$acat_pval),
  ps3 = as.vector(ntc_our$p_value),
  title = "Negative control p-values"
)
```

## Comparison of wilcoxon test, ranked t test and t test

```{r}

# Convert to vectors
wilcoxon_vec <- as.vector(as.matrix(resample_normal_wilcoxon))
rankt_vec <- as.vector(as.matrix(resample_normal_rank))

t_vec <- as.vector(as.matrix(resample_normal_not_rank))

# Calculate correlation
corr_val <- cor(wilcoxon_vec, t_vec, use = "complete.obs")
corr_val_2 <- cor(wilcoxon_vec, rankt_vec, use = "complete.obs")
corr_val_3 <- cor(t_vec, rankt_vec, use = "complete.obs")
plot(wilcoxon_vec, rankt_vec,
     main = "Wilcoxon vs ranked t",
     xlab = "wilcoxon",
     ylab = "ranked t")
# Plot
text(x = 0.55, y = 0.55, 
     labels = paste0("cor = ", round(corr_val_2, 4)), 
     col = "red", cex = 1.2)
plot(wilcoxon_vec, t_vec,
     main = "Wilcoxon vs t",
     xlab = "wilcoxon",
     ylab = "t")

# Add correlation text in red
text(x = 0.55, y = 0.35, 
     labels = paste0("cor = ", round(corr_val, 4)), 
     col = "red", cex = 1.2)

plot(t_vec, rankt_vec,
     main = "t vs ranked t",
     xlab = "t",
     ylab = "ranked t")
# Plot
text(x = 0.55, y = 0.55, 
     labels = paste0("cor = ", round(corr_val_3, 4)), 
     col = "red", cex = 1.2)
```
The wilcoxon test, in principle, is equivalent to ranked t test. However, in implementation, the way I rank the expression data is different (specifically, dealing with ties). For wilcoxon, I use standard wilcoxon ranking i.e. when ties occur, take the mean of the rank. However in ranked t I implemented, I take the minimum of the rank.
But still they are highly correlated.

```{r,echo=F}
      }

      module_names <- c(module_names, module_name)
    }
  }
  
    # Store results as a data frame in the list
  module_results[[i]] <- data.frame(

  )
```

# Apr 2025 - Morris-50 Hallmark gene sets: Different grna assignment strategies affects the Morris results.

We compare 3 configurations: EM Algorithm; cutoff=4; author threshold.

For author threshold, we analyze two options:

1. The total UMI & gRNA counts in the cell (including those gRNA where UMI are below threshold)
2. The UMI & gRNA counts that are above threshold only

For example, in the raw count matrix, gRNA 1 has 5 reads in a cell (above threshold); gRNA 2 has 2 reads in a cell (below threshold), then the first strategy consider number of gRNA as 2, total UMI as 7, whereas the second strategy consider gRNA as 1, total UMI as 5. In this dataset, I found that the first strategy is not inflated, but the second strategy does introduce inflation.


## Sceptre NTC Analysis: genewise p values

For sceptre, we found that the inflation exists in all cases, except author threshold where we only consider gRNA UMI count that are above threshold provided by the author:

**Author threshold (for cell covariates grna_n_umis & grna_n_nonzero, we only consider those above threshold)**

```{r,echo=F,cache=F}
knitr::include_graphics("images/author_adjusted.png", error = FALSE)
```

**Author threshold (for cell covariates grna_n_umis & grna_n_nonzero, consider all UMIs and guides)**

```{r,echo=F,cache=F}
knitr::include_graphics("images/author_corrected.png", error = FALSE)

```


**EM (consider all UMIs and guides)**
```{r,echo=F,cache=F}
knitr::include_graphics("images/EM.png", error = FALSE)

```

**cutoff4 (consider all UMIs and guides)**
```{r,echo=F,cache=F}
knitr::include_graphics("images/cutoff4.png", error = FALSE)

```

We found that for Morris data, Author threshold with covariates that consider gRNA UMI counts that above threshold gives best calibration.

```{r,echo=F}
      # Check if module_p_values still has values after removing NAs
      if (length(module_p_values) > 0) {
        # acat_pval <- ACAT(module_p_values)
        
     acat_pval <- combination.test(
  module_p_values[!is.na(module_p_values)],
  weights = NA,
  method = "Cauchy",
  tail.idx = 1
)


        module_acat_pvals <- c(module_acat_pvals, acat_pval)
        module_names <- c(module_names, module_name)
      } else {
        module_acat_pvals <- c(module_acat_pvals, NA)
        module_names <- c(module_names, module_name)
      }
    } else {
      module_acat_pvals <- c(module_acat_pvals, NA)
      module_names <- c(module_names, module_name)
    }
  }
  
  # Store results as a data frame in the list
  module_results[[i]] <- data.frame(
    grna_id = grna_id,
    module = module_names,
    acat_pval = module_acat_pvals
  )
}


# Combine all results into a single data frame
module_results_sceptre <- do.call(rbind, module_results)
module_results_sceptre <- module_results_sceptre[!is.na(module_results_sceptre$acat_pval), ]

  rownames_to_column(var = "grna_id") %>% # Add row names as a column
  pivot_longer(cols = -grna_id, names_to = "module", values_to = "p_value")

# Remove rows with NA p-values

max_stat_long <- max_stat_long %>%
  semi_join(module_results_sceptre, by = c("grna_id", "module"))

module_results_sceptre$bh_pval <- p.adjust(module_results_sceptre$acat_pval, method = "BH")
module_results_sceptre$identifier <- paste(module_results_sceptre$grna_id, module_results_sceptre$module, sep = "_")
```

```{r,echo=F}
     acat_pval <- combination.test(

)


        module_acat_pvals <- c(module_acat_pvals, acat_pval)
        module_names <- c(module_names, module_name)
      } else {
        module_acat_pvals <- c(module_acat_pvals, NA)
        module_names <- c(module_names, module_name)
      }
    } else {
      module_acat_pvals <- c(module_acat_pvals, NA)
      module_names <- c(module_names, module_name)
    }
  }
  
  # Store results as a data frame in the list
  module_results[[i]] <- data.frame(
    grna_id = grna_id,
    module = module_names,
    acat_pval = module_acat_pvals
  )
}
```

```{r,echo=F}
  # Initialize an empty list to store ACAT p-values and module names for each module
  module_acat_pvals <- c()
  module_names <- c()
  matched_targets <- grna_target_data_frame_omit[grna_target_data_frame_omit$grna_id %in% grna_id, ]$grna_target
  cis_genes <- discovery_pairs_cis[discovery_pairs_cis$grna_target == matched_targets, ]$response_id      
  # Iterate over each module in gene_modules to combine p-values using ACAT
  for (j in 1:ncol(gene_module_index_matrix)) {
    
    
    module_name <- colnames(gene_module_index_matrix)[j]  # Get the module name

    module_genes <- rownames(gene_module_index_matrix)[gene_module_index_matrix[, j] == 1]
module_genes <- intersect(module_genes, colnames(p_values_row))
    
      module_genes <- setdiff(module_genes, cis_genes) 
    
    # Only apply ACAT if there are genes to combine and they are not NA
    if (length(module_genes) > 0) {
      module_p_values <- as.numeric(p_values_row[module_genes])
      module_p_values <- module_p_values[!is.na(module_p_values)]  # Remove NAs
      
      # Check if module_p_values still has values after removing NAs
      if (length(module_p_values) > 0) {
        # acat_pval <- ACAT(module_p_values)
        
     acat_pval <- combination.test(
  module_p_values[!is.na(module_p_values)],
  weights = NA,
  method = "Cauchy",
  tail.idx = 1
)


        module_acat_pvals <- c(module_acat_pvals, acat_pval)
        module_names <- c(module_names, module_name)
      } else {
        module_acat_pvals <- c(module_acat_pvals, NA)
        module_names <- c(module_names, module_name)
      }
    } else {
      module_acat_pvals <- c(module_acat_pvals, NA)
      module_names <- c(module_names, module_name)
    }
  }
  
  # Store results as a data frame in the list
  module_results[[i]] <- data.frame(
    grna_id = grna_id,
    module = module_names,
    acat_pval = module_acat_pvals
  )
}
```

```{r,echo=F}


gene_module_index_matrix <- readRDS("/project/xuanyao/jiaming/Getting_started/data/Morris/program_data_nature_cNMF/gene_module_index_matrix.rds")
grna_target_data_frame_omit <- readRDS("data/Morris_adjusted/program_data/grna_target_data_frame_omit.rds")


discovery_pairs_cis <- readRDS("/project/xuanyao/jiaming/Getting_started/data/Morris_adjusted/program_data/discovery_pairs_cis.rds")


max_stat <- read.csv("/project/xuanyao/jiaming/Getting_started/output/Morris/system_comparison/em/cNMF/resample_normal_test_statistics.csv",row.names = 1)


sceptre <- rbind(readRDS("/project/xuanyao/jiaming/Getting_started/output/Morris/sceptre_all_pairs/em_corrected_cov/results_run_discovery_analysis.rds")[,c(1,2,7)],
                 readRDS("/project/xuanyao/jiaming/Getting_started/output/Morris/sceptre_all_pairs/em_corrected_cov/results_run_calibration_check.rds")[,c(1,2,7)])

sceptre <- sceptre[!is.na(sceptre$p_value), ]
sceptre$p_value[sceptre$p_value == 1] <- 1 - 1e-6

sceptre_wide <- sceptre %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = response_id, values_from = p_value) %>%
  as.data.frame()

# Set the row names to be the grna_id and remove the grna_id column
rownames(sceptre_wide) <- sceptre_wide$grna_id
sceptre_wide <- sceptre_wide[, -1]

sceptre_wide <- sceptre_wide[rownames(max_stat)[rownames(max_stat) %in% rownames(sceptre_wide)], ]

sceptre_wide <- sceptre_wide[, rownames(gene_module_index_matrix), drop = FALSE]


library(eulerr)




module_results <- list()

# Iterate over each row of t_gene_p_no_approximation to compute ACAT p-values for each module
for (i in seq_len(nrow(sceptre_wide))) {
  grna_id <- rownames(sceptre_wide)[i]
  p_values_row <- sceptre_wide[i,] 
  
  # Initialize an empty list to store ACAT p-values and module names for each module
  module_acat_pvals <- c()
  module_names <- c()
  matched_targets <- grna_target_data_frame_omit[grna_target_data_frame_omit$grna_id %in% grna_id, ]$grna_target
  cis_genes <- discovery_pairs_cis[discovery_pairs_cis$grna_target == matched_targets, ]$response_id      
  # Iterate over each module in gene_modules to combine p-values using ACAT
  for (j in 1:ncol(gene_module_index_matrix)) {
    
    
    module_name <- colnames(gene_module_index_matrix)[j]  # Get the module name

    module_genes <- rownames(gene_module_index_matrix)[gene_module_index_matrix[, j] == 1]
module_genes <- intersect(module_genes, colnames(p_values_row))
    
      module_genes <- setdiff(module_genes, cis_genes) 
    
    # Only apply ACAT if there are genes to combine and they are not NA
    if (length(module_genes) > 0) {
      module_p_values <- as.numeric(p_values_row[module_genes])
      module_p_values <- module_p_values[!is.na(module_p_values)]  # Remove NAs
      
      # Check if module_p_values still has values after removing NAs
      if (length(module_p_values) > 0) {
        # acat_pval <- ACAT(module_p_values)
        
     acat_pval <- combination.test(
  module_p_values[!is.na(module_p_values)],
  weights = NA,
  method = "Cauchy",
  tail.idx = 1
)


        module_acat_pvals <- c(module_acat_pvals, acat_pval)
        module_names <- c(module_names, module_name)
      } else {
        module_acat_pvals <- c(module_acat_pvals, NA)
        module_names <- c(module_names, module_name)
      }
    } else {
      module_acat_pvals <- c(module_acat_pvals, NA)
      module_names <- c(module_names, module_name)
    }
  }
  
  # Store results as a data frame in the list
  module_results[[i]] <- data.frame(
    grna_id = grna_id,
    module = module_names,
    acat_pval = module_acat_pvals
  )
}


# Combine all results into a single data frame
module_results_sceptre <- do.call(rbind, module_results)
module_results_sceptre <- module_results_sceptre[!is.na(module_results_sceptre$acat_pval), ]

library(tibble)

max_stat_long <- max_stat%>%
  rownames_to_column(var = "grna_id") %>% # Add row names as a column
  pivot_longer(cols = -grna_id, names_to = "module", values_to = "p_value")

# Remove rows with NA p-values
max_stat_long <- max_stat_long %>% filter(!is.na(p_value))






max_stat_long <- max_stat_long %>%
  semi_join(module_results_sceptre, by = c("grna_id", "module"))

module_results_sceptre$bh_pval <- p.adjust(module_results_sceptre$acat_pval, method = "BH")
module_results_sceptre$identifier <- paste(module_results_sceptre$grna_id, module_results_sceptre$module, sep = "_")
```

```{r,cache=F,fig.width=8.8,fig.height=6}
library(eulerr)

significant_levels <- c(0.01, 0.05,0.1,0.2)
# significant_levels <- 0.01
plot_list <- list()

# Loop through significant levels and display plots
for (significant_level in significant_levels) {
  # Filter significant IDs for each method
```


```{r,cache=F,fig.width=8.8,fig.height=6}
sig_sceptre_author <- na.omit(
  module_results_sceptre_author$identifier[module_results_sceptre_author$bh_pval < significant_level]
)


sig_sceptre_em <- na.omit(
  module_results_sceptre_em$identifier[module_results_sceptre_em$bh_pval < significant_level]
)

sig_sceptre_cutoff <- na.omit(
  module_results_sceptre_cutoff4$identifier[module_results_sceptre_cutoff4$bh_pval < significant_level]
)


  # Prepare the sets
  venn_data <- list(

    `em` = sig_sceptre_em,

    # `wilcoxon_v4` = significant_ids_max_stat_2,
    
   `cutoff4` = sig_sceptre_cutoff,
      `author` = sig_sceptre_author
  )
  
  # Generate the Euler diagram and display it
euler_plot <- plot(
  euler(venn_data),
  fills = list(fill = c( "yellow", "orange","green","red"), alpha = 0.5),
  edges = TRUE,
  quantities = TRUE,
  labels = list(font = 2, cex = 1.2, pos = 3), # 调整字体和位置
  main = paste("Significant level", significant_level)
)
plot_list[[length(plot_list) + 1]] <- euler_plot
}
grid.arrange(grobs = plot_list, ncol = 2)

par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```

```{r,echo=F, fig.height=15, fig.width=15,cache=F}
  geom_point(aes(x = -log10(max_stat_long_2$p_value),
                 y = -log10(max_stat_long_4$p_value))) +
  labs(title = "10000 no approx vs 50000 no approx (-log)",
       x = "-log10(10000 no approx)", y = "-log10(50000 no approx)")

# Arrange plots in a 2x2 grid
grid.arrange(p1, p2, p3, p4, ncol = 2)

```
**Here we find out that there is no significant difference between 10000 resample and 50000 resample; the p values are generally smaller (there are more significant pairs) for ACAT than our method without normal approximation**

```{r,echo=F}
sceptre <- rbind(readRDS("/project/xuanyao/jiaming/Getting_started/output/Morris/sceptre_all_pairs/author_threshold_adjusted/results_run_discovery_analysis.rds")[,c(1,2,7)],
                 readRDS("/project/xuanyao/jiaming/Getting_started/output/Morris/sceptre_all_pairs/author_threshold_adjusted/results_run_calibration_check.rds")[,c(1,2,7)])

  pivot_wider(names_from = response_id, values_from = p_value) %>%

library(eulerr)




module_results <- list()

# Iterate over each row of t_gene_p_no_approximation to compute ACAT p-values for each module
for (i in seq_len(nrow(sceptre_wide))) {
  grna_id <- rownames(sceptre_wide)[i]
  p_values_row <- sceptre_wide[i,] 
  
  # Initialize an empty list to store ACAT p-values and module names for each module
  module_acat_pvals <- c()
  module_names <- c()
  matched_targets <- grna_target_data_frame_omit[grna_target_data_frame_omit$grna_id %in% grna_id, ]$grna_target
  cis_genes <- discovery_pairs_cis[discovery_pairs_cis$grna_target == matched_targets, ]$response_id      
  # Iterate over each module in gene_modules to combine p-values using ACAT
  for (j in 1:ncol(gene_module_index_matrix)) {
    
    
    module_name <- colnames(gene_module_index_matrix)[j]  # Get the module name

    module_genes <- rownames(gene_module_index_matrix)[gene_module_index_matrix[, j] == 1]
module_genes <- intersect(module_genes, colnames(p_values_row))
    
      module_genes <- setdiff(module_genes, cis_genes) 
    
    # Only apply ACAT if there are genes to combine and they are not NA
    if (length(module_genes) > 0) {
      module_p_values <- as.numeric(p_values_row[module_genes])
      module_p_values <- module_p_values[!is.na(module_p_values)]  # Remove NAs
      
      # Check if module_p_values still has values after removing NAs
      if (length(module_p_values) > 0) {
        # acat_pval <- ACAT(module_p_values)
        
     acat_pval <- combination.test(
  module_p_values[!is.na(module_p_values)],
  weights = NA,
  method = "Cauchy",
  tail.idx = 1
)


        module_acat_pvals <- c(module_acat_pvals, acat_pval)
        module_names <- c(module_names, module_name)
      } else {
        module_acat_pvals <- c(module_acat_pvals, NA)
        module_names <- c(module_names, module_name)
      }
    } else {
      module_acat_pvals <- c(module_acat_pvals, NA)
      module_names <- c(module_names, module_name)
    }
  }
  
  # Store results as a data frame in the list
  module_results[[i]] <- data.frame(
    grna_id = grna_id,
    module = module_names,
    acat_pval = module_acat_pvals
  )
}

# Combine all results into a single data frame
```

```{r,include=F}
gene_module_index_matrix <- readRDS("/project/xuanyao/jiaming/Getting_started/data/Morris_adjusted/program_data/manually_created_gene_index_matrix.rds")
grna_target_data_frame_omit <- readRDS("data/Morris_adjusted/program_data/grna_target_data_frame_omit.rds")


discovery_pairs_cis <- readRDS("/project/xuanyao/jiaming/Getting_started/data/Morris_adjusted/program_data/discovery_pairs_cis.rds")


max_stat <- read.csv("/project/xuanyao/jiaming/Getting_started/output/Morris/remove_cis_match_grna/4_cov/HALLMARK_10000_no_approximation/resample_normal_test_statistics.csv",row.names = 1)


sceptre <- readRDS("/project/xuanyao/jiaming/Getting_started/output/Morris/sceptre_all_pairs/author_threshold_adjusted/results_run_calibration_check.rds")[,c(1,2,7)]

sceptre <- sceptre[!is.na(sceptre$p_value), ]
sceptre$p_value[sceptre$p_value == 1] <- 1 - 1e-6

sceptre_wide <- sceptre %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = response_id, values_from = p_value) %>%
  as.data.frame()

# Set the row names to be the grna_id and remove the grna_id column
rownames(sceptre_wide) <- sceptre_wide$grna_id
sceptre_wide <- sceptre_wide[, -1]

sceptre_wide <- sceptre_wide[rownames(max_stat)[rownames(max_stat) %in% rownames(sceptre_wide)], ]

sceptre_wide <- sceptre_wide[, rownames(gene_module_index_matrix), drop = FALSE]


library(eulerr)




module_results <- list()

# Iterate over each row of t_gene_p_no_approximation to compute ACAT p-values for each module
for (i in seq_len(nrow(sceptre_wide))) {
  grna_id <- rownames(sceptre_wide)[i]
  p_values_row <- sceptre_wide[i,] 
  
  # Initialize an empty list to store ACAT p-values and module names for each module
  module_acat_pvals <- c()
  module_names <- c()
  matched_targets <- grna_target_data_frame_omit[grna_target_data_frame_omit$grna_id %in% grna_id, ]$grna_target
  cis_genes <- discovery_pairs_cis[discovery_pairs_cis$grna_target == matched_targets, ]$response_id      
  # Iterate over each module in gene_modules to combine p-values using ACAT
  for (j in 1:ncol(gene_module_index_matrix)) {
    
    
    module_name <- colnames(gene_module_index_matrix)[j]  # Get the module name

    module_genes <- rownames(gene_module_index_matrix)[gene_module_index_matrix[, j] == 1]
module_genes <- intersect(module_genes, colnames(p_values_row))
    
      module_genes <- setdiff(module_genes, cis_genes) 
    
    # Only apply ACAT if there are genes to combine and they are not NA
    if (length(module_genes) > 0) {
      module_p_values <- as.numeric(p_values_row[module_genes])
      module_p_values <- module_p_values[!is.na(module_p_values)]  # Remove NAs
      
      # Check if module_p_values still has values after removing NAs
      if (length(module_p_values) > 0) {
        # acat_pval <- ACAT(module_p_values)
        
     acat_pval <- combination.test(
  module_p_values[!is.na(module_p_values)],
  weights = NA,
  method = "Cauchy",
  tail.idx = 1
)


        module_acat_pvals <- c(module_acat_pvals, acat_pval)
        module_names <- c(module_names, module_name)
      } else {
        module_acat_pvals <- c(module_acat_pvals, NA)
        module_names <- c(module_names, module_name)
      }
    } else {
      module_acat_pvals <- c(module_acat_pvals, NA)
      module_names <- c(module_names, module_name)
    }
  }
  
  # Store results as a data frame in the list
  module_results[[i]] <- data.frame(
    grna_id = grna_id,
    module = module_names,
    acat_pval = module_acat_pvals
  )
}


# Combine all results into a single data frame
module_results_sceptre <- do.call(rbind, module_results)
module_results_sceptre <- module_results_sceptre[!is.na(module_results_sceptre$acat_pval), ]

```

```{r,echo=F,cache=F,fig.width=10, fig.height=7}
ntc_pvals <- module_results_sceptre$acat_pval[grepl("^NTC", module_results_sceptre$grna_id)]
p4<-gg_qqplot(ntc_pvals, title="ACAT, 10*1000=10000 p values")


grid.arrange(p1, p2, p3,p4, ncol = 2)
```
**Comments: I manually created 1000 gene sets by randomly choosing genes (shuffling the rows of gene module index matrix). The reason to create 1000 set is that the discovery set consists of 200*50 pairs, so I want to construct a negative control set with the same size.**

```{r,cache=F,fig.width=12,fig.height=8,echo=F}
library(eulerr)

significant_levels <- c(0.01, 0.05)
# significant_levels <- 0.01
plot_list <- list()

# Loop through significant levels and display plots
for (significant_level in significant_levels) {
  # Filter significant IDs for each method

  module_results_sceptre$identifier[module_results_sceptre$bh_pval < significant_level]
)

  max_stat_long$identifier[max_stat_long$bh_pval < significant_level]
)
#

  max_stat_long_3$identifier[max_stat_long_3$bh_pval < significant_level]
)
# significant_ids_max_stat_4 <- na.omit(
#   max_stat_long_4$identifier[max_stat_long_4$bh_pval < significant_level]
# )


  # Prepare the sets
  venn_data <- list(
    `Sceptre+Cauchy` = significant_ids_gene_wise_p,
     `10000 minp` = significant_ids_max_stat,
    `10000 minp (pooled)` = significant_ids_max_stat_3
        # `10000 minp (normalize sd)` = significant_ids_max_stat_4
    )
  
  # Generate the Euler diagram and display it
euler_plot <- plot(
  euler(venn_data),
  fills = list(fill = c("red", "green", "yellow", "orange"), alpha = 0.5),
  edges = TRUE,
  quantities = TRUE,
  labels = list(font = 2, cex = 1.2, pos = 3), # 调整字体和位置
  main = paste("Significant level", significant_level)
)
plot_list[[length(plot_list) + 1]] <- euler_plot
}
grid.arrange(grobs = plot_list, ncol = 2)

par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```

```{r,echo=F}
  module_acat_pvals <- c()
  module_names <- c()
  matched_targets <- grna_target_data_frame_omit[grna_target_data_frame_omit$grna_id %in% grna_id, ]$grna_target
  cis_genes <- discovery_pairs_cis[discovery_pairs_cis$grna_target == matched_targets, ]$response_id      
  # Iterate over each module in gene_modules to combine p-values using ACAT
  for (j in 1:ncol(gene_module_index_matrix)) {
    
    
    module_name <- colnames(gene_module_index_matrix)[j]  # Get the module name

    module_genes <- rownames(gene_module_index_matrix)[gene_module_index_matrix[, j] == 1]
module_genes <- intersect(module_genes, colnames(p_values_row))
    
      module_genes <- setdiff(module_genes, cis_genes) 
    
    # Only apply ACAT if there are genes to combine and they are not NA
    if (length(module_genes) > 0) {
      module_p_values <- as.numeric(p_values_row[module_genes])
      module_p_values <- module_p_values[!is.na(module_p_values)]  # Remove NAs
      
      # Check if module_p_values still has values after removing NAs
      if (length(module_p_values) > 0) {
        # acat_pval <- ACAT(module_p_values)
        
     acat_pval <- combination.test(
  module_p_values[!is.na(module_p_values)],
  weights = NA,
  method = "Cauchy",
  tail.idx = 1
)


        module_acat_pvals <- c(module_acat_pvals, acat_pval)
        module_names <- c(module_names, module_name)
      } else {
        module_acat_pvals <- c(module_acat_pvals, NA)
        module_names <- c(module_names, module_name)
      }
    } else {
      module_acat_pvals <- c(module_acat_pvals, NA)
      module_names <- c(module_names, module_name)
    }
  }
  
  # Store results as a data frame in the list
  module_results[[i]] <- data.frame(
    grna_id = grna_id,
    module = module_names,
    acat_pval = module_acat_pvals
  )
}


# Combine all results into a single data frame
module_results_sceptre <- do.call(rbind, module_results)
module_results_sceptre <- module_results_sceptre[!is.na(module_results_sceptre$acat_pval), ]
```

<span style="color:red"> We found out that there are some genes with very abnormal null distributions. This is because 1.the number of cells receive the perturbation (SNP-9_1) 2. the number of cells express the genes are very low. </span>

```r
t_test_wilcoxon <- function(response_matrix, grna_assignment_matrix) {


  response_matrix <- t(apply(as.matrix(response_matrix), 1, rank, ties.method = "average"))

  # Step 3: Subtract row-wise minimum
  min_vals <- apply(response_matrix, 1, min)
  response_matrix <- response_matrix - min_vals

  response_matrix <- as(response_matrix, "dgCMatrix")

  if (!inherits(grna_assignment_matrix, "dgCMatrix")) {
    grna_assignment_matrix <- as(as.matrix(grna_assignment_matrix), "dgCMatrix")
  }

  n_cells <- ncol(response_matrix)
  n_genes <- nrow(response_matrix)
  grna_infected_cell_count <- rowSums(grna_assignment_matrix)

  mean_expression_trt <- tcrossprod(grna_assignment_matrix, response_matrix) / grna_infected_cell_count

  grna_control_cell_count <- n_cells - grna_infected_cell_count


  total_expression <- Matrix::rowSums(response_matrix)

  mean_expression_control <- t(total_expression - t(mean_expression_trt * grna_infected_cell_count)) / grna_control_cell_count


  mean_expression <- total_expression/ncol(response_matrix)
  mean_expression_squared <- rowSums(response_matrix^2)/ncol(response_matrix)


  var_expression <- mean_expression_squared-mean_expression^2


  t_statistics <- t(t((mean_expression_trt - mean_expression_control)/sqrt(1/grna_infected_cell_count+1/grna_control_cell_count)*n_cells/(n_cells-1)) / sqrt(var_expression))

  return(t_statistics)
}
```


This will result in a situation in resampling where no cells receiving the perturbation express the genes, leading to an extreme null z value.

This can be proved by the another finding that the presence of abnormal null distribution is strongly correlated with the number of cells express the gene.

**Comparison of wilcoxon test and NB test**

As there are some cases when Sceptre gives significant p value but wilcoxon does not, to see whether it is test method that leads to this difference, we developed our own NB test. Then, under the exact same resamples, we compare the difference between wilcoxon test and NB test.
